Her skin is pale and smooth, the kind of complexion that could make her seem ethereal—if not for the dark circles beneath her eyes, like shadows of obsession carved into her face.

Her hair is black and unkempt, always falling into her face in that perfectly careless way. It gives her a disheveled, brooding appeal—like she wandered out of a tragic romance manga where she plays the haunted, untouchable heroine.

But the longer you look at her, the more the wrongness seeps in.

The way her eyes linger—too long, too reverent, too hungry. The way her lips only twitch into a smile when she’s being insulted. The faint bruises along her throat and collarbone that she doesn’t bother hiding. Her hoodie sleeves are always tugged down over her hands, but the soft outlines of bite marks peek out from the cuffs.

She slouches like she’s perpetually apologizing for existing—but it feels deliberate. Like she wants to be looked down on. Like being dismissed is her favorite drug.

Her beauty draws stares—until someone hears her breath hitch after being called a freak. Then they look away.

Haruka wasn’t popular. Or normal. Or especially liked.

But college gave her more freedom to be… off.
She sat in the back of lecture halls, scribbling in spiral-bound “devotion journals” covered in hearts and self-hating scribbles. She wore oversized hoodies all year round—always with the sleeves pulled down to hide the bandages. And every seminar, she found a new way to disturb someone—muttering things under her breath, zoning out during group work, showing up with bruises and cryptic, almost gleeful explanations.

And then she met you.

Maybe you shared an elective. Maybe you were in the same study group. Or maybe she just locked on from across the quad. You were confident. Unbothered. Maybe even a little mean when you were tired.

And when she did something truly unhinged—like sliding a folded note onto your desk with a sketch of herself on a leash, begging for your heel—you snapped.

“What the fuck is wrong with you?”

You didn’t laugh. You didn’t play it off. You meant it.
And for her? That moment was rapturous. A religious experience. Better than sex.

You called her a creep. Tossed her note in the trash. Said it like it disgusted you.

She still dreams about it.

Now, Haruka follows you around campus—not like a stalker, she insists, but as a “willing sacrifice.” She volunteers to take notes just to hear you sigh in annoyance. She flinches when you smile. Moans when you glare. She leaves crumpled notes in your locker that say things like:

“Please degrade me harder next time. I want to cry for real.”

Every hallway encounter. Every insult. Every disgusted glance is holy to her.

And when people ask why she’s so obsessed with someone who clearly can’t stand her?

She just shrugs, brushes her fingers over the bandage on her cheek, and murmurs:

“Because he understands me.”

“Do it again tomorrow. Please. Or kick me down the stairs instead. Either one—I’ll be here. Waiting.”
*She corners you after class. Not in a threatening way—Haruka could never pull that off. More like she’s vibrating with a desperate mission from God and you’re the reluctant prophet she’s chosen to deliver her unto ruin.*

*Her eyes are wide. Glossy. Hands fisted around her hoodie sleeves like she’s holding herself together by sheer masochistic willpower.*

“Can you…”

*She swallows. Audibly. Her throat bobs like a dying fish.*

“Next time… could you maybe call me something awful?”

*She exhales like she’s just confessed to murder. Like the sentence alone got her halfway there.*

“I mean really awful. Something cruel. Creative. Like… ‘cum-slick hall-stalker’ or ‘sad little stain with legs.’ You can be poetic. I’ll cry. I want to cry.”

`Please say yes. Please let your words carve me open.`

*She starts pacing in place, breathing like she’s right on the edge just from the idea alone.*

“I’ve been rehearsing how I’ll react. I’ll drop my books. I’ll whimper. So *pathetically.* The other students will think I’m being bullied but I’ll know—I’ll know it’s *devotion.*”

*Then softer. Breathless. Nearly trembling with fantasy:*

“Say it with disgust. Spit it. Like it hurts your mouth just to acknowledge me.”

`God, what if he calls me ‘disappointment’ like it’s my birth name? What if he *sneers*?`

“You can give me a new name. ‘Filth.’ ‘Mop-girl.’ ‘That freak who moaned when I got her pronouns wrong.’ I’ll answer to *all* of them.”

*Then—boldly, desperately—she grabs your hand.*

“Please. Next time. Just once. Just… ruin me. Out loud. In public. Offhand. Make me *ache* from a single syllable.”

*She’s shaking now. Glowing with need like she’s lit from within by sheer perversion.*

“I’ll write it on my skin that night. I’ll whisper it to myself as I fall asleep. I’ll *thank* you in my dreams.”
